title: Replying to @Chinyere Obasi #broadway #musicaltheatre #theatre #plays...
transcript: why is the director John Doyle my nemesis? well let's get into it if you don't know John Doyle is a fairly prominent theater director and for the record I don't have anything against him personally I don't know the man a lot of actors have worked with him many times so maybe he's lovely but his direction is very much not my cup of tea he's maybe best known for his Broadway revivals of company, The Color Purple, and maybe most of all, Sweeney Todd which full disclosure I actually didn't see a lot of people associate him with this thing he sometimes does where the actors play their own instruments although most of his productions actually don't do that and it has nothing to do with why I don't like him to me John Doyle ….how do I put this politely he lacks the basic storytelling skills that form the foundation of a director's job there's a fun little phrase I invented to describe my experience watching any John Doyle production which I call the Doyle Daze the Doyle Daze is where I'm in the audience and I feel like I'm in some sort of weird blurry trance where I have this vague awareness that something is happening in front of me on stage but I can't bring myself to be interested or even quite follow it because in a John Doyle production everything takes place in this nebulous wishy washy limbo of space and time we have very little sense of where we are how much time is passing scenes just kind of run together in a confusing way without much sense of pacing or focus and it doesn't even feel abstract in like an interesting experimental way it feels like a lackadaisical, hands-off approach to communicating the story to the audience and here's the thing: a lot of people watching this might be confused because you only know John Doyle from his most successful, highly publicized productions but were you there in the trenches with me when he was at Classic Stage? and I don't mean did you pop in from time to time to catch the popular shows like Assasslns or Carmen Jones I mean were you there for Macbeth? Arturo Ui? Allegro? Cradle Will Rock? Fire and air? tell me if I'm wrong but I'm guessing most of his defenders did not have to slog through that dreary chapter of New York City theater history and frankly even some of his more high profile stuff like I think he ruined Kander and Ebb’s The Visit and I think he gets kind of undue credit for shows like Assassins, Carmen Jones, and The Color Purple where I did enjoy them but mostly in spite of his direction rather than because of it which brings me to the other question you might be wondering which is that if I hate his direction so much why did I keep going back? and I do actually have a concrete answer to this which is that for everything I don't like about his direction he does select interesting material and cast compelling actors I think his production of Color Purple was good mostly just because of how great the performances were his production of Macbeth was probably the worst I've ever seen but Corey Stoll's performance in the title role was maybe the best I've ever seen we have Raul Esparza in Arturo Ui Anika Noni Rose in Carmen Jones Andre the Shields as Touchstone in As You Like It like come on how is this supposed to resist? and then like think about the reason his name came up in my last video it was about shows that are rarely produced that I wanna cross off my list and because of John Doyle I have been able to cross off shows like a man of No Importance Cradle Will Rock and Pacific Overtures which I am grateful for even if it came at a cost
